title: When and how to call an ambulance
what: How to know it is time to call an ambulance, and what to tell the dispatcher. Call your local emergency number.
why: For dangerous situations: chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, loss of consciousness, heavy bleeding, or a serious injury.
duration: talking to the dispatcher usually takes 1 to 3 minutes; arrival time depends on urgency and location
tell_doctor: Age and condition: are they awake, are they breathing
The exact address: entrance, floor, door code

prepare.title: Numbers
prepare.text: Know your local emergency number by heart, and save it in your phone.

prepare.title: At home
prepare.text: Keep the patient's documents and medicine list in one place.

prepare.title: Meeting the crew
prepare.text: If possible, have someone open the door and meet the crew outside.

bring: A list of medicines, or the packs
Discharge papers and ECGs, if you have them
steps: Call emergency services and speak calmly
Say what happened, the person's age, and the address
Do not hang up until you are told you can
Follow the dispatcher's advice until help arrives
Open the door, put away dogs, and have documents ready
feel: Feeling panicked is normal. The dispatcher will guide you with questions
Do not leave out the key facts: are they breathing, are they awake
after: The ambulance crew will examine the person and give care
If needed, the person will be taken to hospital
If they stay at home, ask for advice
red_flags: Chest pain or pressure lasting more than a few minutes: call emergency services
A drooping face, a weak arm, or slurred speech: call emergency services right away
Trouble breathing, or the person is unconscious: call emergency services
Heavy bleeding or a serious injury: call emergency services

faq.q: Can the ambulance refuse to come?
faq.a: When life is at risk, an ambulance is sent. Describe clearly what is happening.

faq.q: Can I give medicine before help arrives?
faq.a: Ask the dispatcher. They will tell you what you can do.

faq.q: What do I do if I see stroke signs?
faq.a: Call emergency services right away, and note the time it started. This matters for treatment.

reminders.text: Know your emergency number. When you call, say what happened and give the exact address.
